items.title: Spurs Notes: Paris Mini-Camp, Arena Project, Popovich, Seahawks
items.content:
The Spurs published a photo on Tuesday (via Twitter) showing the group of players who are in Paris, France this week for a summer mini-camp. The workouts, hosted by Victor Wembanyama, also feature De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, Carter Bryant, Harrison Barnes, Jordan McLaughlin, and offseason addition Tobias Harris.

According to Jared Weiss of The Athletic, big man Kelly Olynyk is also in attendance, though he’s still an unrestricted free agent after spending last season in San Antonio.

Spurs CEO RC Buford revealed during a recent appearance on a French podcast that “eight or 10” Spurs would be joining Wembanyama in France for the offseason mini-camp. Buford observed that it’s a promising show of leadership from a 22-year-old who has established himself as the face of the Western Conference champions.

“The thing that you see about great leaders is very seldom do they resemble or match somebody else,” Buford said, per Michael C. Wright of ESPN. “He’s not trying to be anybody but himself. He sets a great example in his approach, in the way he takes care of his body, the way he connects with his family and with his teammates. There are not many times where 10 guys from a team are flying halfway around the world to go work out together. That’s done because of the respect, admiration and joy that Victor brings.”

We have more on the Spurs:

San Antonio Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones will host three listening sessions regarding a possible $489MM contribution from the city for a new downtown arena, according to Tony Castro of KSAT. City residents may get to vote on the potential deal in November. Buford issued a statement this week noting that Bexar County voters approved $311MM for the project last year, Molly Smith of The San Antonio Express-News writes in a subscriber-only story. He argues that the city only needs approval from council, which happened last August when seven members authorized a draft financing plan for the arena project.
In a recent interview, Buford stated that president of basketball operations Gregg Popovich continues to make progress in his recovery from the stroke that forced him to end his coaching career, per Raul Trey Lopez of The Express-News. Popovich was frequently around the team during its run to the NBA Finals, offering feedback and encouragement throughout the playoffs. “He continues to rehab with more purpose and diligence than I think any of us could have imagined,” Buford said. “He’s improving and, you know, his presence is always there to support the team.”
Head coach Mitch Johnson, a Seattle native, recently took members of his coaching staff to the Seahawks’ training camp to learn more about how the defending Super Bowl champions are preparing for the season, per Tom Orsborn of The Express News. items.title: Jaylen Brown dishes on relationship with Jayson Tatum in Sixers introduction
items.content:
Holding his first press conference since he was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers, star forward Jaylen Brown stressed that he’s moving on from his time with the Boston Celtics.

He didn’t shy away, however, from hints that his final days there weren’t without challenges.

During a Twitch stream in early July, Brown had said he felt there was “a bit of a lack of respect” during trade talks and discussions of Brown’s future, adding that he “wasn’t thrilled” with the way Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens “facilitated some of the conversations.”

When asked Thursday, Aug. 6 what bothered him about his final days with the Celtics, Brown wanted to look forward.

“The whole process,” Brown said. “But to be honest, my mind is so focused on what’s in front of me. I’m moving on. Maybe one day we can share the details of how everything transpired and all the moving parts that took place in this. Obviously, it’s a lot of speculation; I feel no need to chime in on it because I’m focused on what’s in front of me.”

Brown did say that he looks back on his time as a Celtic with gratitude from the city and how it helped him develop as a person. Brown also added the he’ll continue to be active in the Boston community.

Brown revealed that when he first learned of the trade from Boston to Philadelphia, he threw his phone across the room, though he did not elaborate on the emotions behind that.

There has been speculation that the relationship between Brown and Celtics star Jayson Tatum had become strained. The two were teammates in Boston for nine seasons, and the pair won the 2024 NBA Finals, with Brown winning Finals Most Valuable Player.

“We won a championship together,” Brown said when asked how he would characterize his relationship with Tatum. “So anybody that you win a championship with, you would think that’s a brotherhood or a life-long legacy would entail. Obviously, there’s ups and downs in any relationship, for sure. But on my end, there’s nothing but respect. Besides when he plays the Sixers, I hope he does well. But other than that, everything for me is just based in respect.”

When asked if the two had been able to talk, Brown responded: “Not really.”

The 76ers and Celtics completed the trade July 1, with Philadelphia sending Paul George, two first-round draft picks and two second-round selections back to Boston.

“People attacked my character,” Brown added. “Someone even went as far and said I had a disease. So it has been a crazy transition, to be honest. But none of it is completely surprising, even though some of these things were said externally. Internally and through the organization, there had been conversations. I wasn’t that surprised.”
